Tulsa property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Tulsa

  • Tulsa County Assessor handles assessment.
  • Tulsa County Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

Tulsa County Treasurer page: at least one half of the tax must be paid before January 1 (first half cannot be accepted after Dec 31); taxes of $25 or less must be paid in full before Jan 1; if the first half is chosen, the second half must be paid before April 1.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Tulsa County Assessor FAQ: 30 calendar days from the date of the Notice of Valuation to file a written protest with the county assessor (form by mail, in person, or emailed to informalprotest@tulsacounty.org; phone (918) 596-5100); a protest may also be filed if value did not change on or before the first Monday in April; unresolved protests go to the Board of Equalization (formal appeal). Assessor Important Dates page: Board of Equalization adjourns May 31 unless extended to June 30. Statewide . See the official page.

Tulsa by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts about 412,322 people in Tulsa, which makes it the 2nd largest of the 16 ok places we cover. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $189,600, 6% below the median of those 16 places. 52% of occupied homes are owner-occupied and 48% are rented, against a median of 59% owner-occupancy across the ok places. The median home was built in 1972, about 51 years ago, which matters for roofs, plumbing and inspection requests. These numbers describe Tulsa as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
